title.value: Capacity Variation in the Many-to-one Stable Matching
title.justification: The title is directly provided in the paper details, indicating the primary research focus.
title.quote: Capacity Variation in the Many-to-one Stable Matching

extractions.description: The paper investigates the computational complexity of optimally varying hospital capacities in many-to-one stable matching markets. It focuses on how capacity changes impact residents' allocations, both for capacity expansion and reduction. The study proves the NP-completeness of finding optimal capacity variations and explores theoretical foundations through algorithmic and polyhedral approaches.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily addresses theoretical aspects of computational complexity in matching markets, such as school choice and hospital-resident allocation, which are not inherently tied to climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The many-to-one stable matching problem provides the fundamental abstraction of several real-world matching markets such as school choice and hospital-resident allocation.
